## What I found

Gate E (`architecture-as-code`) cannot run on this subject. Its input contract takes only an explicit `Enforcement` handoff from `architecture-guidelines` or `morphogenetic-architecture`; "where the subsystem sits has not been decided yet" means no such handoff exists. Alchemy states the same constraint from the other side: E stays blocked until Gate 3 records a final topology decision. The record calls this **Blocked** — a focused alias reports the missing artifact and stops rather than widening into the pipeline.

Two things placement decides, both of which change the rules rather than decorate them:

1. **Whether notifications is a subsystem or an aspect.** If it is an aspect (one obligation, one mechanism, every other subsystem routes through it — the shape `audit` has in §3), the rules are exclusivity edges `from: '*', except: ['notifications-mechanism'], to: 'notifications-internal-*'`. If it is a subsystem, the rules are layer/tier edges. There is no rule set that is correct under both readings.
2. **Where the afferent rules live.** "Who may import notifications" belongs in the composing parent's file (§4), and the parent is unknown. Its own file may legally name only `notifications-*` and `*` (Directive 3), so the half of the rule set that matters most cannot be placed at all yet.

Separately: this worktree contains only `.claude/skills/` and `CLAUDE.md` — no source, no `package.json`, no `pyproject.toml`, and no assembler. `Stack: Other`, so even the config encoding (`eslint.architecture.mjs` vs `architecture.toml`) is undetermined.

## Why it matters

Writing the rules now means guessing the placement and encoding it in a lint config. Directive §6 wants rules before implementation code precisely so the first wrong import fails on day 1 — but rules guessed ahead of the topology decision do the opposite: they either rubber-stamp whatever placement someone later chooses, or they get rewritten, and the rewrite is indistinguishable from "the rules were in the way." If I guess "aspect" and it lands as a layered subsystem, the exclusivity edges forbid legitimate imports and get deleted wholesale.

Not acting costs one Gate 3 pass. Nothing is blocked downstream: no implementation code exists to govern yet, so there is no window in which ungoverned notification imports can accumulate.

## Do this first

1. Run `/alchemy L notifications subsystem` to get the placement decision (Domain / tier / layer, or an aspect-with-mechanism finding). If it returns `MOVE`/`SPLIT`/`MERGE`/`INTRODUCE-BOUNDARY`, it emits a provisional `DEFER` with a candidate and the handshake continues through C before E unblocks.
2. Bring the resulting `Enforcement` handoff back to `/alchemy E`; I will write the own-file efferent rules plus the parent's afferent rules in one pass.
3. Name the stack when you do (JS or Python), so the config lands as `eslint.architecture.mjs` or `architecture.toml` rather than pseudo-schema.

If you want the full design pass instead of just placement, `/alchemy notifications subsystem` routes `ADAPTIVE` through M, A, L, C, E.

## What I did not check

- Whether notifications is worth building at all — Gate M did not run; `/alchemy M notifications` closes it.
- Any requirements grounding for notifications (actors, obligations, delivery guarantees) — not read, and no requirement artifacts exist in this worktree to read.
- The stack-specific skills `architecture-as-code-javascript` / `-python` — not loaded, since no stack is determined.
- No verification command run; there is no assembler or lint config in this repo to run one against.
